prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: decision support for wildfire detection and suppression in WUI terrain. Architecture: fixed ridge sensors, staffed portal, advisory analytics, comms preserving incident command authority. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall) presents incident info, recommendations and status to authorized personnel. North Lookout Camera Mast (northern rim; drainages, roads, ignition corridors) and South Lookout Camera Mast (opposing viewshed, overlap where terrain blocks north) each have hardened power, cabinets, lightning protection and service access. Video backhauled via licensed wireless links to operations network; cellular is the degraded-mode path. North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet after local processing finds a candidate heat signature. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock and Drone Tasking Service give aerial observation. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine and Smoke Classifier Module screen imagery (advisory only). MesoWest Weather Fusion Node gives weather context. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater bridges digital and field radio. Crewline Mobile Tablet gives mobile access to approved info. Tanker base: Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console, East and West Retardant Loading Pumps. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (warnings, roads, shelters, EOC); Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion) monitors cues, requests verification, recommends escalation, may recommend Confirmed Ignition State only when observations and procedures support it; Air Attack Supervisor; Tanker Base Manager; Helitack Crew Leader and Drone Pilot Operator (field conditions, timing, crew hazards). States: suspected ignition, Confirmed Ignition State, Airspace Restricted State (coordinate aviation/drones). Detection support: observation, automated screening, operator review, presentation of confidence/location/context; ends when an authorized role accepts, rejects or requests verification. Suppression support: resource movement, aviation planning, field safety, fire behavior assessment, safety pauses. Requirements: no autonomous dispatch, independent command decisions or direct control of aircraft, vehicles, pumps, cameras, drones or crews; command authority stays with incident command; system limited to info presentation, procedural support, traceable recommendations, coordination aids.

New part:
S031: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is referred to by the site engineering alias Kestrel in drawings and maintenance records for this deployment.
S032: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is located on a graded pad near the central ridge road so that launch, recovery, charging, and shelter functions remain accessible to maintenance personnel.
S033: The dock includes weather-rated enclosures, charging interfaces, local health monitoring, and a secure network termination for coordination with the rest of the support system.
S034: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock produces the Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records that a flight battery has reached the configured replacement threshold.
S035: Drone Tasking Service manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, and presents task status without acting as an independent authority for flight release.
S036: The Drone Pilot Operator uses Drone Tasking Service to review proposed routes, current dock status, and operational constraints before coordinating any field action through established procedures.
S037: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine is referred to by the site engineering alias Lantern in architecture diagrams and configuration work orders.
S038: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine aggregates camera detections, weather inputs, geospatial context, and operator feedback into traceable recommendations for fire detection and suppression support.
S039: Smoke Classifier Module runs as a bounded analytics component that scores visual observations for plume likelihood and passes confidence values to the broader analytics workflow.
S040: The analytics services retain event timing, source identifiers, model version information, and operator acknowledgments so that later review can reconstruct how a recommendation was presented.
S041: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node is referred to by the site engineering alias Brindle in network inventory and integration test records.
S042: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and configured quality checks to provide a consistent weather picture for the operating area.
S043: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node sends the Wind Shift Bulletin when its configured weather rules identify a significant change in local wind behavior.
S044: VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides a monitored bridge between selected radio traffic and operator workstations, with recording and access controls aligned to incident policy.
S045: Caldera Incident Command Portal is the primary operator interface for the Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, and other command staff who need consolidated situational information.
S046: The portal displays camera views, detection history, weather context, map layers, and status transitions such as Confirmed Ignition State and Airspace Restricted State.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
